questions: How many devices did you measure, and how many showed high-field supercurrent? Table S1 and Section F list GH1 to GH4 plus one non-moiré junction, with GH1 and GH2 showing the effect; could you also give the number of junctions per chip (Fig. S1a shows several contacts on one mesa) and of cooldowns, and say whether "multiple additional devices" (p. 3) means more than GH2?
Why were the others set aside? You give a reason for GH3 and GH4 (SI F, p. 33); were any other junctions fabricated or measured and not reported?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown, in particular the hole-side minibands (n/ns < −1) at high field, the full field range of Fig. 2a, and negative fields?
What does the second-best dataset look like? GH2 appears in Fig. S13; how do interference patterns in GH1 at densities other than n/ns ∼ 1.8 compare with Fig. 2c and Fig. S11?

How was the 3447 Ω series resistance (SI A.2, p. 19) calibrated, and how much do the pockets in Fig. 2a and the 1/R map with its 20 mS cutoff (Fig. 3e, Fig. S18) change if that value moves by a few tens of ohms?

Do the dV/dI vs I maps at high field, over the full current range, show finite-bias resonances (multiple Andreev reflection or self-induced steps), and do they move with field together with the switching current?

Could you extract Jc(x) from the high-field interference patterns (Fig. 2c, Fig. S11), as you did near zero field in Fig. S9, to show whether the high-field supercurrent flows through the bulk or near the edges?
Does the normal-state map taken at 200 nA (Fig. S14) show the same correlation with ⟨v²⟩/vF² as the zero-bias 1/R map in Fig. 3e, and how were the 20 mS cutoff and the ⟨v²⟩/vF² > 0.1 level chosen?
